learning: Iteration 1 showed line loss of 1 per run at max_error about 0.061 m, so reach was the bottleneck. Next, if line loss is 0 and max_error still reaches 0.06 m, test turn authority through wheel_track or mass.
notes: Seven-sensor package with 20 mm spacing and a 120 mm total span. The controller is unchanged from iteration 1 so the race isolates sensing reach.
rationale: The Builder's iteration 2 geometry is seven sensors at x = -0.060 to +0.060 m (20 mm spacing), 16 mm footprints, y = 0.03 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, mass 0.8 kg. Iteration 1 measured line loss of 1 per run and max_error of about 0.061 m on the 72 mm span, so the sensor reach was the first thing to test. I keep the controller identical to iteration 1 (kp 2.0, ki 0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.4, last_direction) so that this race isolates the geometry change. The weights are proportional to sensor x, scaled to about 1 per 30 mm, so the signal stays within the ±2 limit: [-2, -1.333, -0.667, 0, 0.667, 1.333, 2]. Iteration 1 scored 56.2 against 79.6 in iteration 0. Its s-bend progress fell from 0.29 to 0.18, so the narrower track and shorter lead may have cost more than the wider span gained. This package therefore tests reach alone, and the next iteration can separate the track and lead effects. Expected result: line_loss_events near 0 and max_error below 0.06 m. The risk is that the seven-sensor signal becomes more sensitive to edge crossings and raises steering_oscillation.
